CweFindings.Name: Use of Obsolete Function
CweFindings.Description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.
CweFindings.Explanation: Serializing.SerializeBinary and DeserializeBinary instantiate and call BinaryFormatter (lines 11-12 and 19-21). BinaryFormatter is an obsolete serialization API in modern .NET and remains in this shared utility, creating a compatibility and maintenance risk.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogDBInitializer.GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence (line 329) and CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue (line 23) explicitly cast the SQL Int64 sequence result to int. Values outside the Int32 range are truncated, producing incorrect identifiers.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Calculation
CweFindings.Description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Index accepts pageSize and pageIndex from request parameters without range checks (lines 22-25). CatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated multiplies them in pageSize * pageIndex at line 29; large values can overflow the Int32 calculation and yield incorrect pagination offsets.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: ApplicationModule.Load registers CatalogServiceMock as SingleInstance when mock data is enabled (lines 18-22), but its per-instance mutable catalogItems list is accessed by request methods without synchronization.

CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogServiceMock.catalogItems is mutable shared state (line 12); CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem modify it (lines 48-67), while read methods access it concurrently, with no synchronization.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: The singleton CatalogServiceMock exposes concurrent collection reads and mutations without a lock or other synchronization, allowing overlapping requests to observe or modify inconsistent list state.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Locking
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogServiceMock uses a singleton mutable list without acquiring a lock in its CRUD/read operations, so callers can concurrently alter the resource.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: Autofac shares CatalogServiceMock across request scopes when mock mode is enabled (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22), but list access and mutation in CatalogServiceMock.cs:19-67 are unsynchronized.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: Although CatalogItemHiLoGenerator uses a lock, CatalogServiceMock does not synchronize access to its shared catalogItems list; concurrent create, update, delete, and read operations can race.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create and CatalogController.Edit bind PictureFileName from submitted model data (lines 62 and 100). PicController.Index combines that persisted value with the Pics directory at line 39 and reads the resulting path at line 44 without verifying it remains under the directory. A crafted filename can therefore escape the intended Pics directory.

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit accept a user-supplied PictureFileName (lines 62 and 100). PicController.Index passes the stored value directly to Path.Combine at line 39 and then reads the file at line 44, without normalizing or constraining traversal sequences such as ../.

CweFindings.Name: Absolute Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit accept PictureFileName from submitted data (lines 62 and 100). PicController.Index uses it as the second argument to Path.Combine at line 39; an absolute filename can replace the Pics root, and the resulting path is read at line 44.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit bind PictureFileName from request data (lines 62 and 100). PicController.Index uses that value to identify the file resource via Path.Combine at line 39, then reads it at line 44 without restricting it to the Pics directory. This is the same confirmed file-resource path used in the file-path assessment.
